subject.title: fix: Teams Graph and media work with RFC2544 proxy DNS

question: After a real host-proxy run demonstrates the intended behavior, should OpenClaw accept this narrowly host-scoped RFC2544 exception for the Teams plugin?
rationale: The code changes a security boundary: whether RFC2544 proxy DNS is an acceptable exception for approved Microsoft endpoints is a maintainer policy decision, not something focused mocks can settle.

options.title: Require proxy-runtime proof, then accept the narrow exception
options.body: Obtain redacted evidence for Graph and media traffic through the intended host proxy, then merge only if the hostname-scoped boundary remains intact.

options.title: Keep RFC2544 blocked
options.body: Reject the exception if maintainers do not want proxy DNS in the benchmark range to bypass the default SSRF classification, even for approved Microsoft hosts.

recommendation.title: Require proxy-runtime proof, then accept the narrow exception
recommendation.body: Obtain redacted evidence for Graph and media traffic through the intended host proxy, then merge only if the hostname-scoped boundary remains intact.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current policy implementation and can provide the most direct technical context, though historical ownership evidence is limited.
